newsitem.title: INDIA: India's BJP says will not try to form government.
newsitem.headline: India's BJP says will not try to form government.

text.p: India's main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said on Monday that it would not seek to form a fresh government.
"There is no question of the BJP forming a government at this stage," BJP leader Atal Bihari Vajpayee told reporters after meeting President Shankar Dayal Sharma.

The BJP's chances of making a new claim to rule were boosted on Sunday when Congress, the second biggest party, announced it was withdrawing support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority coalition government.
The rightwing Hindu nationalist BJP is the largest single party in the lower house of parliament and with its allies controls 194 votes in the 545-seat chamber.
It held power for 12 days last May after inconclusive general elections but Vajpayee was forced to resign as prime minister when his party failed to muster enough support to win a vote of confidence.
But the main opposition party is known to favour mid-term elections which a recent opinion poll said could strengthen the BJP's hand in parliament.
President Sharma on Monday asked Deve Gowda to seek a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament by April 7.
Asked how the BJP would vote, Vajpayee said the party had called a meeting for April 6 of its parliamentary members. "We will decide after that," he said.
